Commentary.Commentary: Since the start of Sri Lanka's second innings, their batters looked unfazed by the three-bowler pace attack of South Africa. They made them toil with consistent partnerships, scored at a brisk rate and kept the only threat, Keshav Maharaj, out as well. This match is set up for their win and only a miracle could save the visitors now. Their second innings starts in a short while, hang around!

So, after 18 overs in this session, Sri Lanka have finally decided to end South Africa's misery in the field. They lost Angelo Mathews for 71 in this session just before drinks, however, the wickets were never going to bother them. They have piled on a lead of 489 and set a humongous total for the visitors. Keshav Maharaj after much await got his 12th wicket of the match and ended the second innings with the figures of 40-4-154-3, bowling a total of 81 overs in this match.

Suranga Lakmal is waving his hands from the balcony and he is calling his players back which means only one thing - SRI LANKA HAVE FINALLY DECLARED! The tired South African team walks back quicker because their opening duo does not have much time as it has to come out to bat quickly.
On the pads and worked to the on side for a run by Dickwella.

That is a superb piece of fielding by Kagiso Rabada. It is landed outside off, the ball from de Bruyn, that is, Silva first comes forward and then rocks back to play the shot. It is on the leg stump and he works it fine. Rabada runs after it, puts in a slide and stops it just inside the fence to save a run for his team. Pommie Mbangwa on air mentions - 'Tell you what-  that is the first time I am seeing Kagiso Rabada slide..' is it????
Rocks on the back foot to push it to covers.
Niroshan works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Rocks back and cuts it through cover-point for a run.
FOUR! Too full and Dickwella isn't going to miss out on these. He gets forward and drives it through the empty cover region. A boundary results.

Casual from Bavuma at second slip to allow the batters to change strike. A shortish delivery around off, Silva looks to guide it past slip but wasn't able to. However, a misfield from Bavuma there allowed them to take the run.
Cheeky Niroshan is into the act. He looks to play the ramp shot and gets it off the splice off his bat to fine leg. One run taken.
Floated around off, pushed to the off side.
Dickwella leaves the first ball outside his off stump.
Niroshan Dickwella comes out to bat.
Drinks!

OUT! Finally! What a marathon it has been for Maharaj. He has been on that off stump channel consistently. The batsman played and missed on so many occasions but this time, he has his target. He should be a relieved man with sore fingers. A flighted delivery around off, he gets Mathews forward and induces the outside edge of his blade. Du Plessis takes a diving catch to his right and rests on the ground with a happy face. A 64-run partnership has been broken by Keshav Maharaj who gets his 12-fer in his 81st over of the match.
Down the leg side, Silva misses the flick.
The batsman offers no stroke and is wrapped on the pads.
Flatter in line of the stumps, punched to mid on for a run.
On middle, tucked to the on side for no run.
Mathews is late to play the off spinner but does well in the end.
Slow off spin on off, Mathews punches it to short mid-wicket for no run.
Gets behind the line and bunts it out.
Theunis de Bruyn is on.
Fuller around off, driven to covers for no run.
Roshen chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Silva has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Worked to mid on. One run taken.
Driven through mid off by Angelo.

Pushed through by Markram, Mathews drives it to mid on for a run.
Hangs back to push it away. No run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full, driven to covers.

Now Silva chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

On the pads, flicked through the on side for a run.
Markram goes around the wicket, Silva flicks it to mid-wicket.

The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Slower and short, negated off the back foot.

Copy-paste stuff from the bowler and the batsman.

The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.

Flatter on middle, Angelo wrists it away to the on side for nothing.
On the pads, defended.
Rocks back and punches it through covers for another run. I am not really sure how many runs Sri Lanka really want on this pitch. It is already more than enough. Worth 466 now to be precise...
Mathews lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Drives this one to covers for a run.
He looks to cut the fuller ball and misses it again. Silva hasn't looked convincing but he is still out there in the middle though.
A tad shorter outside off, cut to point for no run.
Another play and miss to the ball around off.
Tucked through the square leg region by Silva to bring up the 250 for his team.

Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Ha ha... something different to talk about other than just block and leave. Russel Arnold has a chat with Pommie Mbangwa on air, regarding superstitions - where to sit, how to sit, etc... A certain Sourav Ganguly will have something to say about that - if you remember, some 17 years ago, in 2001, when the 'invincible' Aussie team had landed on Indian shores - about to seal the Test series At Eden Gardens, Kolkata - Ganguly sat shirtless on the balcony of the Indian dressing room, with his upper torso covered only by a towel. This, he maintained he did, so that India do not lose a wicket. The result? Australia went wicketless the whole of Day 4!!! The rest, as they say, is history. Not promoting superstition but one of those #justsaying things...

The bad day, match and tour continues for South Africa. They struggled this morning as well, with Lungi Ngidi getting the lone wicket. Maharaj got some turn but nothing else to show for the other bowlers. 'Sri Lanka can do what they wish after Lunch!' exclaimed a joyful Russel Arnold on air. Indeed, they can. It is a matter of when they declare now. Join us back at 1240 local (0710 GMT) for the second session...

Angelo Mathews and Dimuth Karunaratne started the proceedings well to put up 63-run stand but the latter got out on 85 to miss out on a well deserved century. Then, Mathews joined hands with Roshen Silva to keep the bowlers at bay. He got to his 28th fifty as well and helped extend the already extended lead to 451.

He has now conceded 261 runs in this Test - MOST BY A SOUTH AFRICAN BOWLER IN A TEST MATCH - going past Imran Tahir's 0/260 against Australia in Adelaide in 2012. Well, at least Keshav has 11 wickets to show in this case...

Pitch report - Shaun Pollock and Kepler Wessels are reporting from the middle. They say that the pitch has dried up even more, puff of dust is coming off from the surface when the ball lands and it's going to assist spinners more than the fast bowler. Kepler asserts that the Sri Lankan spinners will be looking forward to bowl on this track and the batting is going to be difficult. Pollock ends by saying if nothing works, the sweep will be the best option.

Hello and welcome to the third day of the second and final Test match between Sri Lanka and South Africa at Sinhalese Sports Club, Colombo. The home team is on top. It went through the Proteas' line-up on Day 2 and extended its dominance with more runs on the board. The lead has swelled up to 365 runs, which is more than handy. The interesting thing now is to see when will they declare and put South Africa in to bat. There are two more days left in this Test, but perhaps we might not require them considering the state of the pitch right now. The play gets underway in a short while, hang around!
... Day 3, Session 1 ...
That's all from us on Day 2. Will there be a Day 4 in this Test remains to be seen! But Day 3 is certain. You can join in for that which begins at 1000 local (0430 GMT). Enjoy your weekend, cheers!

It's all Sri Lanka for the moment. If they had enforced the follow-on, maybe the game would have got over early on Day 3. South Africa will have to try and figure out a way to get the hosts bundled out and at least put up a fight in their last innings. Looking at the way they batted throughout the series, one would say there doesn't seem to be much scope for them.

The technique of 'how to play spin on these sub-continent pitches' will have to be answered by the South African batters. It took just 34.5 overs for the home team to get them all out. Akila Dananjaya picked up his 2nd 5-wicket haul and Dilruwan Perera gave him good company taking 4 wickets. For the visitors, only their skipper Faf du Plessis and keeper Quinton de Kock showed some intent with the bat. The rest were just mentally not prepared to tackle spin as there was just one fifty-plus stand. Earlier in the day, Rangana Herath and Akila Dananjaya pilled on 74 runs for the last wicket and stretched their team's total to 338.

If not the first, the second day is surely won by Sri Lanka. They outplayed the visitors in all the departments to get more than an upper hand in this game. The openers once again gave them the headstart stitching 91 together. Dimuth Karunaratne who became just the fourth Sri Lankan to get 4 back-to-back fifties in each Test innings is showing some character. Kusal Mendis ran himself out but the former skipper, Angelo Mathews ensured Sri Lanka did not slip further.

Played to the point region by Dimuth.
Gets behind the ball and taps it to the off side.
FOUR! The Sri Lankan batters are attacking Maharaj more in the second innings. Mathews makes room and lofts this beautifully over covers. A boundary.
DK has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Played with soft hands towards square leg for a run.
Milks this through mid on for an easy run.
Loopy ball on leg, tucked away to the on side.
Karunaratne has flicked the ball off his pads.
FOUR! Class, pure class! Overpitched ball around off, Mathews leans forward and unleashes the cover drive to perfection.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Lands it full once again on off, pushed to covers.
Length outside off, cut away to the point region.
Fuller this time on middle and off, driven back to the bowler.
Length ball outside off, well blocked by Mathews.
Lungi Ngidi comes on for his first over this innings.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Angelo has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single. He is off the mark.
Angelo Mathews is the new man in.

OUT! A wicket against the run of play. Miscommunication between the batters and Mendis is well short of his mark. A short ball from Maharaj outside off, he rocks back and places his shot in the deep extra cover region. They jog for the first, complete the second and suddenly, think they can get the third run as well. However, Kusal is then sent back by his partner in his stride. Markram in the deep throws the ball back to the keeper after mopping up it from the fence. De Kock stretches his arm to dislodge the bails. The umpire takes it upstairs and even a dive couldn't save Mendis. Sri Lanka lose their third wicket but it shouldn't worry them too much as they are already in the driving seat.
Now then! A run out appeal is been referred up. De Kock thinks he has his man. Kusal Mendis is waiting in anticipation.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! No one in the deep and Mendis adds another boundary to his name. Takes on the preditable Maharaj and plays an inside out shot over the cover region.
Flat ball on leg, Karunaratne rocks back and pulls it in front of square. Will get just the one for it.
Fuller on leg, flicked away to square leg for a brace.
Tries to york him as he bowls a fuller ball on middle, Kusal hits it towards mid on.
Outside off, Mendis plays it to the off side.
Outside off, Kusal gets behind it and taps it down.
Length outside off, Mendis blocks it with a straight bat.
Steyn bangs it short first up, Dimuth pulls it through mid-wicket for one.
Loopy ball on middle and leg, played towards mid on.
Flighted ball on off, DK pushes this towards mid on and jogs to complete the run.
Sharp turn down leg, Karunaratne flicks it to the square leg fielder.
Works this towards square leg for a run.
Prods forward and taps it in front of him.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for Dimuth.

FOUR! Fourth fifty in a row for Dimuth and his 17th overall in this format. What a series he is having. Another fuller ball from Steyn on off, Karunaratne drives it in the gap through cover-point to get to the landmark.
Another ball driven towards that region.
Pushed to the cover region by DK.
Karunaratne lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Pitched up ball on off, Dimuth drives it to covers.
Covers his stumps and blocks this ball comfortably.
Defended off the front foot by Mendis presenting the full face of the bat.
Kusal has flicked the ball off his pads.
FOUR! Another one! This time with the turn. On the up, not an easy shot to play. Tossed up ball from Maharaj around off, Kusal lofts it uppishly towards extra cover for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! They have been playing the sweep so very well. Fetches this from outside off and slogs it through mid-wicket. No fielder there and no one to chase the ball either. Boundary.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another fuller ball on off, driven to covers. Sri Lanka's lead now is 326 runs.
Fuller this time outside off, pushed to the cover region.
FOUR! Delicately done. Waits for the ball to come to him and cuts it late past the backward point fielder. A boundary.
Digs this short on middle, Karunaratne is not in total control and looks to pull it away. He misjudges the bounce and gets hit on his shoulder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length ball on that fourth stump channel, Karunaratne is happy to defend the ball.
Tickles this to the on side to retain strike for the next over.
FOUR! That will get him to 44. Comes dancing down, takes it on the full and drives it towards extra cover. No fielder there and he will get his boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Turns his bat to the leg side for nothing. Dot ball.
Comes down the track and works it to mid on.
Length outside off, Kusal shows Steyn the sticker of his bat maker.
Stays back once again and shows his solid defense.
Covers his stumps and blocks it with a straight bat.
Hangs back in his crease and bunts it down.
Good length ball outside off, Kusal looks to cut it but cannot put bat to ball.
Length ball around off, Mendis hits it back towards the bowler.
Half-tracker on middle, Karunaratne pulls this to mid-wicket.
Drives this towards the off side for a run.
Sharp turn. Mendis hangs back and looks to block it but gets beaten.
Mendis gets behind the ball and blocks it.

OUT! No bat and de Silva has to take the long walk back. A great review from South Africa and Maharaj gets another one. Loopy ball on leg, just like the previous ball. Once again de Silva comes down looking to work it on the on side. The ball spins back in and hits de Silva low on his back leg. A strong appeal from the bowler but the umpire stays put. They have a chat and Faf takes it upstairs. Replays show us that there was no bat and the ball would have gone on to hit the middle of middle stump. Also, Kusal Mendis is the next batsman in...
An LBW decision is taken up. South Africa look confident. But, is there a bat?
Tossed up ball on leg, de Silva comes down the track and looks to flick it but gets hit on the pads. Appeal to no avail.
A lot of air on this one, DK waits for it to play it off the back foot.
Misses to play this one and gets hit on his pads.
FOUR! Another short ball and punished by Karunaratne this time. He rocks back and pulls this one to the square leg fence.
A touch short in length, Karunaratne defends it off the back foot.
Comes down the track to play this one. He gets it to mid on uppishly.
Shorter on middle, eased through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Karunaratne has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! A wicket on the previous ball and Karunaratne brings out the sweep. Fetches it from outside off and sweeps it over backward square leg for a boundary.
Drinks have been taken! Also, Dhananjaya de Silva walks out to bat.

OUT! Finally a wicket for South Africa. They have been made to work for it and Maharaj is the man once again. 10-fer for the left-arm orthodox spinner. He gives this one air on middle and leg, Gunathilaka dances down the track and looks to clear the infield. Can't get hold of it and finds Elgar at deep cow corner who runs to his right and dives to take a very good catch.
Uses his feet and works this towards cow corner. Another comfortable brace.
Flicks this through mid-wicket for a brace.
Around off, blocked!
FOUR! Lead is 300 now! Gunathilaka reverse sweeps the full ball once again and finds the gap through the cover-point region. Innovation to get to the landmark!
Fuller ball driven through covers by Karunaratne. Lead swells to 299.
Gets behind the line of this one and defends it down the track for nothing.
A tad shorter and slower from de Bruyn, blocked off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wide outside off stump, Gunathilaka leaves it alone.
Sweeps the full ball through square leg and takes a brace.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and connects.

FOUR! Fortune favors the brave and Gunathilaka has been! He looks to cut the faster ball but ends up getting an outside edge. The ball evades the keeper's gloves and the first slip fielder moved the wrong way to let it pass between the two. A boundary through the third man fence to get to his 2nd fifty. Lead is getting bigger and bigger for SL.
Some air on this one, Karunratne gets to the pitch of the ball and punches it through long on. Another single taken.
Comes down the track and gets it through long on. A run taken.
Aiden Markram is back on.
On the leg side, worked fine by Karunartne. Two runs results.
Shows the full face to the flatter ball and keeps it out.
Hangs back to the shortish ball and pushes it off the back foot.
On the pads, flicked to the on side by Dimuth.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Comes ahead to play it to the off side.
Theunis de Bruyn is on.

SIX! In the air... and it's a SIX! Elgar made a mess of it. Markram bowled a flighted ball outside off, Gunathilaka slogs it aerially to the mid-wicket fence. Dean standing there misjudges it first, comes in from the fence and is late in getting back. He ends up missing it altogether. The ball lands directly on the ropes. Nothing going SA's way.
Around off, Gunathilaka lunges forward once again but doesn't get his bat behind the line cleanly.
Lunges forward and blocks it out!
In line of the stumps, defended off the back foot down the track for nothing.
Another full ball and another sweep shot. This time he gets it to mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller, swept but couldn't get it past FSL.
Short and wide, cut through backward point by Gunathilaka. A misfield from the fielder there allows them to take two.
Slower around off, Karunaratne puts it in the gap through cover-point for a single.
Comes down the track this time and plays it to the off side.

Edge but safe! A flighted ball on a length, Gunathilaka pushes hard at it and gets it off the outside edge through the third man region. Amla runs after it from first slip and keeps the batters under three.
In line of the stumps, defended back to the bowler.
Flighted on middle, driven through covers for a brace by Gunathilaka.
Makes his way down the track to this flighted ball and knocks it down to long on for one.
Works it away with the spin on the leg side. No run taken.
Plants his front foot forward and meets it with a straight bat in defense.

Big appeal for an lbw, but correctly shut down. Flighted outside off, it spins in and catches Gunathilaka on the pads as he moves a long way across his stumps. Impact clearly outside off, could see all three sticks.
Sweeps this full ball behind square on the leg side for a single.
Quicker through the air outside off, it turns in, Dimuth moves across and blocks it out.
Fullish around off, defended off the front foot by Gunathilaka.
On the pads, worked to the on side for no run.
A full toss from Aiden, Gunthilaka pushes it straight to the short cover fielder.
A full toss from Aiden, Gunthilaka couldn't get it past the short square leg fielder.
A tad shorter, defended.
Hangs back and bunts it out. Markram is easier to handle considering the Lankan batters play better spin in the nets.
Mistimed reverse sweep goes to the point region.
On the pads, flicked through the leg side for nothing.
Flatter around off, it spins back and hits the batsman on his pad. The fielding team asks the question but the umpire denies it again.
FOUR! Out comes the slog sweep once again. Most potent weapon for most of the batters. A flighted ball around off, Karunaratne gets down on his knee and smashes it through the wide long on region.

Good fielding effort this from Elgar to save a run for his team. Gunathilaka flicks this one off his pads and gets it fine. The ball races towards the fence but Elgar runs after it, puts in a timely dive in the deep and saves a run for his team. He knows the value of each and every run! 50-run stand comes up between the duo.
Charges down the track to get to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Moves away from his wickets and punches it through covers. One run taken.
Copy-paste stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
Lunges forward to the tossed up ball and blocks it down the track.
Fuller on off, drive to mid off for no run.
Pushes this one around off, it pitches and spins away just a tad from the left-hander. Gunathilaka tries to poke at it but misses.
Aiden Markram is into the attack as the second spinner.
Dimuth offers no stroke and is rapped on the pads. The fielding side is asking the question. The umpire decides the batsman is not out as it might have been missing the sticks.
Moves away from his stumps to play it off the back foot through cover-point. One run added to the total.
Gunathilaka fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad.
Flatter outside off, Gunathilaka gets forward to block it.

Ooh! Clever, very clever from Maharaj. He saw Gunathilaka coming down the track and hence, he fired this one outside off. But kudos to the batsman who saw this plot and got his foot back in time. Good stuff this.
Swept handsomely through deep square leg for a brace. It's all too  easy for the Lankan batsmen right now.
Drives the full ball through covers. The fielder at mid off scampers to his right and stops it but not cleanly. Two runs taken.
Hangs back to the back of a length ball and eases it through the on side for a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Another short ball around the grille area, Karunaratne pulls it to mid-wicket for another run.
Follows the short ball with a length ball. Karunaratne pushes it through mid on.
Short around the shoulder height, pulled through mid-wicket for no run.
Tossed up on length and it spins away from the leg stump. Gunathilaka looks to flick but it misses everything it seems and thuds into de Kock's gloves. Maharaj appeals but the umpire ignores it.
Wide down the leg side, No trouble at all for the batsman.
Faster in line of the stumps, kept out to the on side.

SIX! Some more intent this time. He is the aggressor in this innings for the home team. A tossed up ball on middle and off, Gunathilaka gets down on his knee and slogs it over mid-wicket fence. A maximum results!
Comes charging down the track to block this one. He is showing intent.
Flatter on a good length, worked to through square leg. One run taken.
Short of a length again, played to the on side for no run.
On the hips coming in with the angle, pushed to the on side for a run.
A back of a length delivery targeting the rib cage, Gunathilaka hops and gets it to mid on for a run.
Kagiso goes 'round and Danushka gets it away from his crease.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Rabada goes over the wicket to angle it across and manages to beat Gunathilaka's willow on the outside.
FOUR! Bang! Shot and it's a no ball as well. But Gunathilaka has no qualms in playing his shots. He drives it on the up through mid off and the ball races to the fence for a boundary.
Gunathilaka has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Loopy ball down leg, Gunathilaka gets on one knee and looks to paddle sweep this. Gets a faint edge to this and the ball trickles down towards the fine leg region for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Just over Rabada! Gunathilaka picks up the length early, gets into position and reverse sweeps this over backward point. Boundary.
Turned around the corner for nothing.
Off spinner down leg, Gunathilaka tries flicking the ball but misses.
Gets off the inner half back to the bowler.
Oh! Over the off pole. The length ball cuts back and evades the under edge of Karunaratne's bat. No harm done in the end.
Short outside off, he looks to pull but misses it. He looks in some hurry. Perhaps SL want to put SA into bat as early as possible.
And now gets beaten off the length ball. He looks to cut it fiercely but connects with thin air.
Around off this time but similar leave from Karunaratne.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Edge but safe! It was on a good length around off, Dimuth gets an outside edge and it goes through square on the off side for a boundary.
Carefully tackled off the back foot by Gunathilaka.
Hangs back and bunts it out the off side.
Flighted around off, Danushka comes forward to play it but gets hit on the pad after missing it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Gunathilaka is no mood to hang around! He gets into the act and whips the slog sweep to the flighted ball bowled around off and gets it through wide long on. A boundary!
Flatter on middle, eased through mid-wicket. One run taken.
In line of the stumps on a back of a length, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, caressed to covers off the front foot.
Drives this one to mid off.
FOUR! Classy. Full in line of the stumps and driven straight down the ground. Impact straightaway!
Another full toss outside off, driven to mid off for another single.
Starts with a full toss, Karunaratne whips it to mid-wicket. One run taken.
Kagiso Rabada is on.
Gets behind the line of the flatter ball and defends it to end the first over.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
On the pads, flicked through square leg for a run.
Hangs back and blocks the ball out to the off side.
Not surprising South Africa starts the innings with spin. But sadly for them, they only have one conventional spin bowler in their playing XI.
Fuller ball on off, driven to mid on for a run.
Starts with a spinning delivery going down the leg side. Danushka fails to make contact.
